SEPARATION AGREEMENT AND GENERAL RELEASE

This Separation Agreement and General Release is made between Halcyon Instruments, Inc. (the "Company") and Marguerite Vance (the "Employee").

1. SEPARATION DATE

The Employee's employment ends on August 31, 2026 (the "Separation Date"). The Employee will be paid all wages earned through that date and all accrued, unused vacation, whether or not the Employee signs this Agreement.

2. SEVERANCE

If the Employee signs this Agreement, does not revoke it, and returns Company property, the Company will pay severance of twenty-six (26) weeks of base salary, $118,750.00 in total, less withholding, in the Company's regular payroll cycles beginning on the first payroll date after the Effective Date. The Company will also pay the employer portion of COBRA premiums for six months or until the Employee becomes eligible for other group coverage, whichever comes first.

3. NO OTHER COMPENSATION

Except as stated above, the Employee is owed no other wages, bonus, commission, equity vesting, expense reimbursement, or benefit.

4. GENERAL RELEASE

In exchange for the severance, the Employee releases the Company and its officers, directors, employees, agents, affiliates, successors, and assigns from all claims the Employee has or may have through the date the Employee signs this Agreement, whether known or unknown, including claims under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Age Discrimination in Employment Act, the Americans with Disabilities Act, the Family and Medical Leave Act, the Employee Retirement Income Security Act, the Fair Labor Standards Act, and the North Carolina Equal Employment Practices Act.

5. WHAT IS NOT RELEASED

This release does not waive: any claim that arises after the Employee signs; any claim for vested benefits under a retirement plan; any right to workers' compensation or unemployment benefits; any right to indemnification or coverage under a directors and officers policy; and any right that may not be waived by law. Nothing in this Agreement prevents the Employee from filing a charge with, or participating in an investigation by, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, the National Labor Relations Board, the Securities and Exchange Commission, or any other government agency, or from receiving an award from a government whistleblower program, although the Employee waives any personal monetary recovery in a charge the Employee files or that is filed on the Employee's behalf, other than such an award.

6. OLDER WORKERS BENEFIT PROTECTION ACT

The Employee is 40 or older. The Employee is advised in writing to consult an attorney before signing this Agreement. The Employee has twenty-one (21) days from receipt to consider it, and may sign before the 21 days end if the Employee chooses. The Employee may revoke this Agreement within seven (7) days after signing by delivering written notice to the Head of People Operations. This Agreement does not become effective or enforceable until the eighth day after signing (the "Effective Date"), and no severance is paid before then. The release does not cover any claim under the Age Discrimination in Employment Act that arises after the Employee signs.

7. RETURN OF PROPERTY

By the Separation Date the Employee will return every Company device, credential, key, card, document, and copy, and will delete Company data from personal devices and accounts.

8. CONTINUING OBLIGATIONS

The Employee's obligations under the Proprietary Information and Inventions Agreement signed on January 8, 2021 continue, and nothing in this Agreement limits them. Nothing in this Agreement or that one prohibits the Employee from disclosing a trade secret in confidence to a government official or an attorney solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law, or in a document filed under seal, as 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b) provides.

9. NO ADMISSION

This Agreement is not an admission by the Company of any wrongdoing or liability.

10. NON-DISPARAGEMENT

The Employee will not make a statement that disparages the Company, and the Company will direct its officers not to make a statement that disparages the Employee. Neither restriction applies to truthful testimony, a communication with a government agency, or a statement about unlawful conduct in the workplace.

11. REFERENCES

The Company will confirm the Employee's dates of employment and title in response to a reference request.

12. GOVERNING LAW AND ENTIRE AGREEMENT

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of North Carolina. It is the entire agreement between the parties on this subject and may be changed only by a writing both sign. If any provision is unenforceable, the rest remains in effect.

13. ACKNOWLEDGMENT

The Employee has read this Agreement, understands it, has had the opportunity to consult an attorney, and signs it voluntarily.

HALCYON INSTRUMENTS, INC.
